claims.claim: A non-domiciled resident is taxed only on foreign income remitted to Malta (summary: dividends left in the US account are not taxed)

sources.name: PwC: Malta, individual, taxes on personal income
sources.says: Last reviewed 30 September 2026. Persons ordinarily resident but not domiciled "are not taxable in Malta on income arising outside Malta, which is not received in Malta", nor on "capital gains arising outside Malta, regardless of whether they are received in Malta". Those with "income arising outside Malta of at least EUR 35,000 or equivalent" are "subject to a minimum tax in Malta of EUR 5,000". Global Residence Programme: remitted foreign income is "taxed at a flat rate of 15%, subject to a minimum tax of EUR 15,000"; the GRP is "set to be superseded by the new Individual Tax Programme Rules, 2026" from 1 January 2027, with a minimum tax of EUR 35,000 for global residents; beneficiaries and applicants filing by 31 December 2026 stay on the current rules until 31 December 2031. Malta Retirement Programme: 15% on remitted foreign income, minimum EUR 7,500 plus EUR 500 per dependant (EUR 15,000 for retired pensioners under the 2027 rules).

claims.note: The pick's `why` ("Malta's remittance basis lets dividends stay in the US account") agrees.
